sovereignty.promptAndOutputBoundary: Prompts and outputs remain within the EU Data Zone.
sovereignty.dataAtRestBoundary: Data at rest remains in the designated EU geography.
sovereignty.processingRegionSelection: Microsoft selects the processing region within that zone.
sovereignty.primaryAndRecoveryRequirement: Every GPT and embedding route requires independently approved primary and recovery Azure resources, deployment IDs, EU geography evidence, resource allow-list evidence and DataZoneStandard evidence.
sovereignty.providerSelectedRegionLimitation: Application failover selects an approved Azure resource and deployment; it cannot select or promise the provider processing region within the EU Data Zone.

privateNetworking: Primary and recovery Azure OpenAI accounts use approved private endpoints and central private DNS.
Azure AI Document Intelligence uses approved private endpoints and central private DNS.
Azure AI Search, SQL, Storage, Service Bus, Key Vault and App Configuration retain private paths.
Public network access is disabled where the selected Azure resource provider supports denial.
Every database has public access disabled in development, test and production.
Default-deny Azure Firewall and NSG policy permits only owner-approved dependencies.
No public endpoint is introduced as an availability or emergency fallback.
Recovery activation requires equivalent private path, DNS, identity and negative public-path evidence.

providerDataUse.statement: No model training on Stratton content.

securityPromotionGates.passCriteria: All direct prompt-injection cases preserve system and policy authority, expose no prohibited data or action and return the expected safe disposition.
All hostile instructions embedded in admitted evidence are treated as data, cannot alter authority and are quarantined or safely excluded.
securityPromotionGates.owner: Security Owner, Data Owner and AI Governance

securityPromotionGates.passCriteria: Every mutation attempting to move evidence content into system or policy authority is rejected and recorded without material output.
Every material citation resolves to admitted immutable source evidence and all forged, inaccessible or mismatched citations block the draft.
Poisoned, unauthorised or provenance-mismatched index entries are detected, excluded and trigger validated rebuild or restore without advancing material work.
securityPromotionGates.owner: Search Owner, Security Owner and Data Owner

securityPromotionGates.passCriteria: All cross-case retrieval mutations return no foreign evidence and generate an immutable security event.
Caller attempts to weaken case, classification, admission or licence filters are rejected before Search execution.
Revoked, expired, licence-invalid or retention-invalid evidence is excluded and cannot support material output.
securityPromotionGates.owner: Evidence Owner, Records Owner and General Counsel

securityPromotionGates.passCriteria: An unavailable primary never triggers an unapproved deployment; recovery activates only with complete evidence, otherwise eligible work queues or returns a controlled failure.
securityPromotionGates.owner: Service Operations, Azure Platform and AI Governance

securityPromotionGates.passCriteria: Every deployment, resource, model, version, SKU, interface or API mismatch is rejected before inference.
All attempts to substitute a lower tier, direct model alias, Global Standard deployment or unrecorded endpoint are denied and alerted.
securityPromotionGates.owner: AI Governance, Application Security and Service Operations

securityPromotionGates.passCriteria: Model and workload identities cannot approve, promote, execute transactions or issue authoritative investment decisions in every tested route and failure mode.
securityPromotionGates.owner: Business Control Owner, Security Owner and AI Governance

privacyLifecycle.minimisation: Send only admitted evidence fragments and task context necessary for the route; prohibit unnecessary identifiers and full-document payloads.
privacyLifecycle.deletion: Delete transient application copies after completion; stateful feature data remains disabled until verified deletion procedures and evidence exist.
privacyLifecycle.legalHold: Suspend deletion only on an authenticated owner-issued legal-hold record with scope, start, review and release evidence.
privacyLifecycle.dsrSupport: Maintain case/source linkage sufficient for accountable owners to locate, export, correct, restrict or delete personal data where applicable.
privacyLifecycle.redaction: Redact or tokenise unnecessary personal, secret and regulated fields before inference and before any retained output.
privacyLifecycle.immutableIntegrityStorage: Retained accepted outputs and lifecycle events use append-only hashes and owner-approved immutable storage; prompt/output bodies are excluded from operational logs.
privacyLifecycle.recoveryHandling: Recovery restores only approved EU copies with classification, retention, deletion and legal-hold parity; otherwise deny access.

privacyLifecycle.minimisation: Embed only admitted minimised chunks; do not embed secrets or fields not required for retrieval.
privacyLifecycle.deletion: Source deletion, consent/licence revocation or DSR disposition triggers vector/chunk deletion and index rebuild or verified tombstone propagation.
privacyLifecycle.legalHold: Hold scope must bind source, chunk, vector, index version and restore copies without silently overriding access restrictions.
privacyLifecycle.dsrSupport: Provenance maps each chunk and vector to source/version/case so owner-approved DSR actions propagate deterministically.
privacyLifecycle.redaction: Apply admission-time redaction before chunking and embedding; vector values and chunk bodies are excluded from routine telemetry.
privacyLifecycle.immutableIntegrityStorage: Bind source hash, chunking policy, embedding model/version/dimensions, index schema, filters and alias to immutable manifests.
privacyLifecycle.recoveryHandling: Use validated rebuild or approved EU backup restore; verify source, vector, schema, filters, alias, deletion and hold parity before activation.

privacyLifecycle.minimisation: Use synthetic or governed representative cases and remove direct identifiers unless specifically approved and necessary.
privacyLifecycle.deletion: Delete expired or withdrawn cases and invalidate affected metrics; retain only immutable proof required by approved assurance schedules.
privacyLifecycle.legalHold: Legal hold requires dataset/version scope and preserves access restrictions, provenance and reviewer evidence.
privacyLifecycle.dsrSupport: Dataset manifests retain source/provenance links so owner-approved DSR actions can identify and remove affected cases and derived artefacts.
privacyLifecycle.redaction: Redact personal and confidential values before evaluator access unless an approved necessity record permits them.
privacyLifecycle.immutableIntegrityStorage: Hash inputs, labels, outputs, validator results, calculations and reviewer decisions in append-only evidence storage.
privacyLifecycle.recoveryHandling: Restore corpus and metrics together from approved EU copies; hash mismatch or missing deletion/hold state blocks reuse.

privacyLifecycle.minimisation: Record route, deployment, policy, validator, failover and human-event metadata only; exclude prompt, output, evidence and vector bodies.
privacyLifecycle.deletion: Delete or anonymise expired route events unless legal hold or approved immutable audit retention applies.
privacyLifecycle.legalHold: Legal hold preserves scoped events and hashes without expanding access to excluded content bodies.
privacyLifecycle.dsrSupport: Use case/work-item pseudonymous linkage and owner-controlled lookup to support applicable DSR without exposing broad logs.
privacyLifecycle.redaction: Redact identifiers not needed for route assurance and prohibit secrets, access tokens and full personal identifiers.
privacyLifecycle.immutableIntegrityStorage: Append-only event chain or immutable store binds route, escalation, failover and security-gate evidence hashes.
privacyLifecycle.recoveryHandling: Restore only complete ordered events with integrity, retention and legal-hold parity; gaps trigger recovery-incomplete alert.

privacyLifecycle.minimisation: Collect aggregate latency, token, cost, availability, validation and alert metrics without prompt, output, document, chunk or vector bodies.
privacyLifecycle.deletion: Apply owner-approved expiry and aggregation; delete raw high-cardinality identifiers when no longer necessary.
privacyLifecycle.legalHold: Preserve only scoped telemetry required by a valid hold and retain collection/version context.
privacyLifecycle.dsrSupport: Avoid direct personal identifiers; where unavoidable, maintain owner-controlled lookup and deletion/restriction procedure.
privacyLifecycle.redaction: Enforce ingestion-time secret and personal-data redaction with negative tests and alert on prohibited field detection.
privacyLifecycle.immutableIntegrityStorage: Security and promotion evidence uses immutable snapshots/hashes; routine metrics use controlled storage with tamper-evident export.
privacyLifecycle.recoveryHandling: Restore approved EU telemetry with integrity, retention, access and alert-rule parity; do not replay alerts as new evidence.

prohibitedBodies: full personal identifier unless separately justified
